title: Go back to the previous build after an upgrade that succeeded, and one build stamp for every binary
purpose: DIRECTORY-045 upgrades a running install and returns to the previous build only when the upgrade itself fails. A build that starts ready and misbehaves an hour later has no way back but hand moves in the install folder, which an ordinary person cannot make. Its build stamp is also four byte-identical build.rs files that a test holds equal: one script copied four times, not one script. Amended 28 September 2026 21:05 by Waffles after Archie's read against the tree.
task: Add `lys identity upgrade --back`, which returns the install to the build kept beside it through the same stop, swap, start and ready path as an upgrade; and move the build stamp into one build-support crate that each binary's build.rs calls. This brief builds on DIRECTORY-045 as re-driven with R5 to R7: config.previous/ and the intent record exist on the base, and --back exchanges configuration and compose with them. A round built on 045's first round, which had only bin/ and surface/, does not meet R1.

requirements.title: `lys identity upgrade --back`
requirements.spec: Behavioural. `lys identity upgrade --back` (the same verb, so there is one path) reads the version of every binary in bin/ and in bin.previous/ before stopping anything, and refuses by name when there is no bin.previous/ (nothing_to_return_to) or a version cannot be read. It then stops the broker and the service through their exit locks, exchanges bin/ with bin.previous/, the configuration and compose files with config.previous/ (DIRECTORY-045 R5) and surface/ with surface.previous/ when that exists, recreating any compose service whose definition changes (so the build it leaves becomes the one kept, and --back again returns to it), starts both and waits on their readiness events, and writes install/build.json. A failure on the way puts back what it moved, exactly as an upgrade does, and names the binary and its log. It never writes data/ or a credential, and it reads and honours an unfinished upgrade's intent record first (DIRECTORY-045 R7). The Build line on the account screen shows the build now running. Each build records the newest data format it writes (the log event kinds it can read, as a format number in install/build.json and its --version detail). Before stopping anything, --back compares the kept build's format with the data's, and when the older build cannot read the data it refuses back_would_not_read, naming the first event kind the older build does not know. Data is never rolled back. The format is never a version line written by hand. Each signed log the service folds has one list of the kinds it decodes, and its decoder matches against that list, so a kind cannot be decoded without being in it: identity changes (the wire constants in crates/lys-identity/src/event.rs, mod wire at line 263, decoded by decode_change in crates/lys-identity/src/encoding.rs at line 272), grant changes (crates/lys-identity/src/grants/events.rs at line 243) and revocation leaves (crates/lys-identity/src/revocation/leaf.rs at line 223). The format a build writes is derived from those lists, and each binary reports it in its --version detail from its own main.rs, so every real build states the format it reads. The exchange never leaves an install without bin/. When both folders exist it is one atomic exchange (renamex_np with RENAME_SWAP on macOS, renameat2 with RENAME_EXCHANGE on Linux). Where a step is a plain rename, a failure undoes the renames already finished before --back returns, and only then does the put-back run. A leftover from an exchange that was interrupted (bin.exchanging or its like) is recorded in the DIRECTORY-045 R7 intent record before the first rename. The next --back or upgrade finishes or undoes it from that record by itself, and never asks the person to move folders by hand. The failure line under --back begins "going back failed", not "upgrade failed".
acceptance: After an upgrade that succeeded, --back leaves the earlier commit running, answering /api/authority with that build, and --back again returns to the newer one.
With no bin.previous/ it is refused nothing_to_return_to and nothing is stopped.
A start failure during --back leaves the build it began from running and names the binary and its log.
After an upgrade whose build writes a new event kind, --back is refused back_would_not_read naming that kind, and nothing is stopped.

A build of lys, lys-identity-server and lys-secrets at this change reports in --version a data format derived from the kinds lists, and adding a kind to a list without changing anything else changes the reported format.
A test that makes the second rename of the exchange fail leaves bin/ holding the build that was running, that build answers /api/authority, and no bin.exchanging is left.
A test that stops --back after its first rename leaves an intent record, and the next --back finishes or undoes the exchange from it with no step by hand.
A failure during --back prints a line beginning "going back failed".

requirements.title: One build stamp
requirements.spec: Structural. A build-support crate, crates/lys-build-stamp, holds the one function that computes the stamp (head commit, `; dirty`, or `not built from a git commit`) and the rerun-if lines. Each of lys, lys-identity-server, lys-secrets and lys-home lists it under build-dependencies and its build.rs is one call. The byte-identity test is removed with the copies; the stamp's own tests (exported tree, fresh commit, dirty) move into the crate and run against it.
acceptance: No two build.rs files in the workspace hold the stamp logic; each is one call.
The crate's tests prove the three stamp forms.
Every binary's --version still prints its name, version and commit.

boundaries: SHALL NOT change what an upgrade writes beyond bin/, bin.previous/, the configuration and compose files and config.previous/, the screens, the logs, the process files, install/upgrade.json and install/build.json; data is never rolled back.
SHALL NOT add a timeout, deadline, poll, #[allow], #[ignore] or any bypass.
SHALL NOT add a silent fallback: every failure is a named refusal.
verification: The full Lys gate, ast-grep scan and surface checks exit 0 at the card's head, measured by the card round.
On a scratch install: upgrade to a newer build, --back, and read the older commit from /api/authority; --back again and read the newer one.
